composition: Position the primary subject or focal element to occupy exactly 40% to 60% of the frame, centered or along a strong diagonal.
Maintain a clear foreground-to-background separation with at least 3 distinct depth planes (e.g., foreground element at 20%, midground subject at 50%, distant background at 30%).
Use extreme low-angle or high-angle forced perspectives to create dynamic scale contrasts between foreground objects and background architecture.
typographie: Place clean, sans-serif text layers strictly within the upper 20% or lower 20% of the frame to avoid overlapping the central logo zone.
Scale text to occupy no more than 15% of the total frame width, ensuring high legibility with pure white (#FFFFFF) or high-contrast fills.
Align text elements to follow the perspective planes of physical surfaces in the midground for integrated environmental typography.
lumiere: Implement dual-temperature lighting: pair a warm golden hour key light (3000K) with a cool, desaturated ambient fill or screen glow (6500K).
Use high-contrast overhead sunlight to cast sharp, defined shadows and create bright rim lighting on the subject's shoulders and hair.
Incorporate realistic light interactions like water caustics, translucent wave glows, and volumetric dust motes in light beams.
etalonnage: Apply a highly saturated palette dominated by vibrant turquoise (#00C2D1, #00A8C6) and deep blues (#004BFF), contrasted against warm sandy tones (#D1B894) or terracotta (#C68B6D).
Maintain a cinematic film curve with low-contrast shadows and creamy, desaturated highlights (#FDFBF7) for historical or retro scenes.
effets: Apply realistic camera depth of field (bokeh) to heavily blur background elements beyond the central 60% focal zone.
Add physical texture overlays including water spray, wake foam, CRT static, and subtle glass reflections on foreground screens.
logo: Reserve the absolute center (a 30% circular zone) as a clean, high-contrast negative space specifically designed to host a logo.
Ensure background elements behind the logo zone are desaturated or blurred to prevent visual interference with the logo silhouette.
interdits: Avoid flat, low-detail textures on large foreground surfaces like umbrellas, concrete walls, or vehicle panels.
Do not use stiff, artificial, or floating character poses that lack realistic contact shadows with the ground or furniture.
Avoid repeating, tiled texture patterns on background buildings or windows.
Do not allow low-polygon modeling or jagged anti-aliasing on prominent foreground objects.
